1.q: Which TWO characteristics are essential to defining a project in APM terms?
o: Temporary nature
Continuous improvement
Uniqueness of deliverables
Repetitive execution
Ongoing operational support
1.w: Projects are temporary and unique endeavours.

1.q: Which TWO situations justify an extended life cycle?
o: Benefits realised over time
Immediate project closure required
Need to track outcomes
Fixed outputs only
No stakeholder involvement
1.w: Extended life cycles suit projects where benefits emerge over time.

n.3: Outputs alone do not justify extension.

1.q: A construction company repeatedly builds identical housing units using the same design and process. Which classification best applies?
o: A project because each house has a defined completion date
BAU because the work lacks uniqueness despite being temporary per unit
A project because each house produces a distinct output
A hybrid of project and BAU due to repetition
BAU only if there are no external stakeholders
1.w: Repetitive work with minimal variation is BAU, even if outputs are discrete.

n.2: Outputs alone do not define projects.
n.3: Classification depends on characteristics, not blending.

1.q: Which TWO elements should a governance decision framework normally clarify?
o: Criteria for comparing options
Personal preferences of the loudest stakeholder
Authority required for different decision types
Exact technical method for every task
The removal of all escalation routes
1.w: Decision frameworks define criteria and authority so decisions are consistent and controlled.

1.q: Which TWO risks are associated with ignoring float in scheduling decisions?
o: Unexpected delays affecting the critical path
Improved flexibility
Misallocation of resources
Reduced project complexity
Shortened timelines
1.w: Ignoring float can lead to resource misallocation and delays impacting critical activities.

1.q: Which TWO actions would strengthen escalation discipline in a project?
o: Define tolerance thresholds at the start
Encourage informal escalation to any senior manager
Clarify who has authority to approve exceptions
Delay reporting until a problem is irreversible
Remove the project manager from decision-making
1.w: Clear tolerances and approval authority make escalation controlled and timely.

1.q: Which action would most effectively reduce project duration when focusing on the critical path?
o: Shortening non-critical activities
Adding float to the schedule
Reducing the duration of critical activities
Increasing contingency
Extending activity durations
1.w: Only reducing critical path durations directly shortens the overall project timeline.

1.q: A project governance board requests assurance reports from an independent reviewer. What is the main purpose of this oversight activity?
o: To replace the project manager's delivery responsibility
To provide confidence that the project is controlled and aligned
To remove the need for stakeholder consultation
To approve every operational decision
To transfer accountability from the sponsor to the reviewer
1.w: Assurance gives governance bodies confidence that delivery, risks and controls remain appropriate.

1.q: A project manager focuses only on the critical path when monitoring progress. What risk does this create?
o: Critical activities may be delayed
Non-critical activities may become critical without detection
The schedule will become inaccurate
Resources will be over-allocated
The project will finish early
1.w: Ignoring near-critical activities risks them becoming critical due to unmonitored delays.

1.q: A delay occurs on a critical activity, but the project completion date does not change. What is the most plausible explanation?
o: The activity was incorrectly identified as critical
Additional resources were added to compensate
Float was available on the critical path
Dependencies were removed
The delay was negligible
1.w: Critical activities have zero float; if a delay does not affect completion, it was not truly critical.

1.q: A project manager escalates a supplier dispute to the sponsor because it threatens delivery tolerances. The sponsor criticises the escalation as unnecessary detail. What is the best assessment?
o: The project manager acted appropriately because tolerances were threatened
The sponsor is correct because supplier issues are never governance matters
The team should resolve all supplier issues without escalation
The dispute should only be reported after project closure
Escalation should be avoided unless costs have already been incurred
1.w: Issues threatening tolerances should be escalated so governance roles can make or support required decisions.

1.q: Which TWO benefits are associated with extended life cycles?
o: Verification of outcomes
Reduced governance
Improved value realisation
Elimination of feedback
Fixed scope definition
1.w: Extended life cycles ensure outcomes and value are realised.

1.q: Which TWO risks arise if an extended life cycle is not used?
o: Unrealised benefits
Improved predictability
Lack of outcome verification
Reduced stakeholder engagement
Faster closure
1.w: Without extension, benefits may not be realised or verified.

n.4: Closure speed is not the main issue.

1.q: Which change is most likely to alter the critical path?
o: Reducing the duration of a non-critical activity with float
Adding resources to a non-critical task
Increasing the duration of a critical activity
Improving communication between stakeholders
Reordering independent tasks
1.w: Changes to critical activities directly affect the critical path and overall duration.

1.q: Which situation most clearly represents a project rather than BAU?
o: Monthly financial reporting using standard templates
Continuous system maintenance and patching
Implementing a new enterprise resource planning system
Processing daily customer orders
Updating employee records in HR systems
1.w: ERP implementation is unique and temporary, aligning with project definition.

1.q: Which TWO situations should normally trigger escalation within project governance?
o: A forecast breach of agreed tolerance
A routine task completed by the team
A decision needed beyond the project manager's delegated authority
A minor update to a team checklist
A planned meeting taking place as scheduled
1.w: Escalation is appropriate when tolerances are threatened or decisions exceed delegated authority.

1.q: Which TWO characteristics define a critical activity?
o: Zero float
Longest duration
Direct impact on project completion
Highest cost
Requires specialist resources
1.w: Critical activities have zero float and directly influence completion.

1.q: A digital transformation initiative is described as ‘ongoing, evolving, and continuously improving processes’. Why is this description problematic when defining it as a project?
o: It lacks clarity on outputs
It suggests absence of governance
It conflicts with the temporary nature required for projects
It ignores stakeholder engagement
It overstates the importance of outcomes
1.w: Projects are temporary; ongoing evolution suggests BAU or programme activity.

n.0: Outputs are not the main issue.
n.3: Stakeholders are not the defining issue.

1.q: Which situation most accurately indicates that an activity is on the critical path?
o: It has the longest duration in the project
It has zero float and directly impacts project completion
It requires the most resources
It is the first activity in the schedule
It is the most complex task
1.w: Critical path activities have zero float and directly affect project duration.

1.q: A programme manager claims a long-running internal reporting initiative is a project because it required initial funding approval and produced a new dashboard. The team now continuously updates reports and adds minor features every month. Which judgement best aligns with the APM definition of a project?
o: It remains a project because it produces outputs that can be enhanced over time
It is a project only if the dashboard continues to evolve in response to stakeholder feedback
It is no longer a project because the work has transitioned into ongoing operational activity
It remains a project because it originally had a defined start and funding approval
It is a project because it involves stakeholders and delivers organisational value
1.w: Once work becomes continuous and repetitive, it shifts from temporary endeavour to BAU, even if it originated as a project.

n.0: Ongoing enhancement does not maintain project status; repetition indicates BAU.
n.1: Evolution alone does not define a project; temporariness is key.
n.3: Historical characteristics do not define current classification.
n.4: Value delivery alone does not distinguish projects from BAU.

2.q: Which TWO statements about float are correct?
o: Float allows flexibility in scheduling
Float exists only on critical activities
Float can absorb delays without affecting completion
Float eliminates uncertainty
Float is fixed throughout the project
2.w: Float provides flexibility and can absorb delays without affecting completion.

2.q: A delivery team proposes three options to recover schedule slippage. The project board chooses the cheapest option without considering risk or benefit impact. What has most clearly failed?
o: Resource planning
Decision quality within governance
Team motivation
Procurement strategy
Technical configuration control
2.w: Governance decisions should consider balanced criteria, not cost alone.

2.q: Which TWO features indicate effective project governance oversight?
o: Regular review of alignment with business objectives
Approval of every minor team-level decision
Monitoring whether tolerances remain under control
Avoiding escalation to preserve delivery speed
Delegating sponsor accountability to the project team
2.w: Effective oversight checks strategic alignment and whether the project remains within agreed controls.

2.q: A project team is tasked with implementing a process used successfully in another division with minimal changes. Which factor most challenges whether this work should be considered a project?
o: The existence of predefined deliverables
The presence of stakeholders across divisions
The lack of uniqueness in the work being performed
The need for formal governance approval
The requirement to deliver within a set timeframe
2.w: Projects require uniqueness; replicating standard processes reduces this characteristic.

n.0: Deliverables exist in both projects and BAU.
n.1: Stakeholders are present in both contexts.
n.4: Time constraints alone do not define a project.

2.q: Which TWO scenarios could cause a change in the critical path?
o: Delays in near-critical activities
Reducing float on non-critical tasks
Increasing duration of critical activities
Improving team communication
Adding contingency to the schedule
2.w: Changes to critical or near-critical activities can shift the critical path.

2.q: A project schedule shows an activity with negative float. What does this indicate?
o: The activity is ahead of schedule
The project is ahead of plan
The activity is delaying the project completion
The activity has no dependencies
The critical path has been shortened
2.w: Negative float indicates that the schedule is behind and the activity is impacting completion.

2.q: Which TWO risks are created by weak governance oversight?
o: Strategic drift from business objectives
Improved decision consistency
Late identification of major issues
Clearer escalation thresholds
Reduced need for assurance
2.w: Weak oversight can allow projects to drift and issues to surface too late.

2.q: A manager describes a project as ‘any work that has a start and end date’. What is the most accurate critique of this statement?
o: It ignores stakeholder involvement
It overlooks the requirement for governance structures
It fails to recognise that temporary work must also be unique
It incorrectly assumes all BAU work is continuous
It overemphasises outputs over outcomes
2.w: Temporariness alone is insufficient; projects must also be unique.

n.0: Stakeholders are not the defining factor.
n.1: Governance is not part of the core definition.
n.4: Outputs vs outcomes is not the central issue.

2.q: An activity on the critical path is completed earlier than planned. What is the most likely impact?
o: The project will automatically finish earlier
The critical path will be removed
The project end date may improve if no other constraints exist
Float will increase across all activities
Other activities will be delayed
2.w: Early completion of critical activities can reduce overall duration if no other constraints limit progress.

2.q: During project initiation, a sponsor emphasises that success will be measured by improved customer satisfaction rather than system deployment. What is this primarily highlighting?
o: Outputs should be deprioritised in favour of deliverables
Outcomes are more significant than outputs in defining value
Projects should not focus on technical deliverables
Customer satisfaction is an operational metric only
Outputs and outcomes are interchangeable in project success
2.w: Outcomes represent benefits and value, whereas outputs are deliverables.

n.3: Customer satisfaction can be a project outcome.

2.q: Which TWO risks arise from poorly defined milestones?
o: Ambiguous progress measurement
Improved stakeholder clarity
Misaligned decision points
Reduced project complexity
Faster reporting cycles
2.w: Poor definition leads to unclear progress and ineffective decision-making.

2.q: A governance group approves a project but does not define decision rights, tolerance limits or escalation thresholds. What is the most likely consequence?
o: The project manager will have clearer autonomy
The project will need less reporting
Decisions will become inconsistent and accountability unclear
The project board will be unnecessary
Stakeholder engagement will automatically improve
2.w: Without decision rights and escalation thresholds, governance becomes inconsistent and accountability weakens.

2.q: A senior user representative is excluded from governance decisions about acceptance priorities. What is the most likely risk?
o: The project manager will lose all delivery authority
The governance board will become too large
Decisions may not reflect user needs or acceptance criteria
Supplier costs will automatically increase
The escalation process will become unnecessary
2.w: Governance decisions need appropriate representation so user needs and acceptance priorities are considered.

2.q: A project delivers a new CRM system, but user adoption remains low and sales performance does not improve. Which statement best reflects the distinction being demonstrated?
o: The project failed because it did not deliver its output
The project delivered outputs but failed to realise outcomes
The project delivered outcomes but lacked defined outputs
The project succeeded because outputs were delivered within scope
The project cannot be assessed without stakeholder feedback
2.w: The CRM system is an output, but improved sales is the intended outcome, which was not achieved.

n.0: The output was delivered; failure relates to outcomes.
n.3: Success requires more than output delivery.
n.4: The distinction is clear without further input.

2.q: A team delivers a software tool exactly as specified, but users adapt it in unexpected ways to generate additional benefits. What does this illustrate?
o: Outputs can directly control outcomes
Outcomes may differ from intended outputs
Outputs and outcomes are independent and unrelated
Outcomes emerge from how outputs are used
Outputs should not be defined at project start
2.w: Outcomes depend on how outputs are applied in practice.

n.0: Outputs do not fully control outcomes.
n.1: Outcomes do not differ from outputs; they are distinct.
